text:
neil (People Ops): @aoife quick one — Conor in Platform messaged me that his July payslip shows both Irish PAYE and UK PAYE withheld for the same pay period after his short-term secondment started. Can payroll check?

liam (Engineer): He DM'd me the stub. He moved 2026-07-10 and payroll ran 07/15. Stub snippet (redacted):
```
Pay period: 07/01/2026 - 07/15/2026
Ordinary pay (IRE): 3,200.00
Secondment pay (UK): 2,400.00
Irish PAYE: ,980.00
UK PAYE: ,860.00
Net: 2,760.00
```
Conor (via DM): I assumed we'd only be taxed in the UK for the period after 07/10. Looks like both jurisdictions took tax on overlapping days.

aoife (Payroll): Thanks. Can you paste last4 or EmpID so I can pull the runs?

neil (People Ops): Conor OConnor, EmpID 54890, last4 2211. Secondment effective 2026-07-10, HR approved 07/02 and local secondment letter sent 07/08.

intl-payroll: Noted. @payroll-bot please fetch payroll records for EmpID 54890 for pay run 2026-07-15 and confirm source of the two earnings lines.

payroll-bot: Pulling payrun 2026-07-15 for EmpID 54890... Found record. Two earnings rows present: 1) IRE-BASE exported by Dublin payroll provider, 2) UK-SECOND exported by central UK payroll integration. Both exports arrived within payroll cutoff window and were ingested into the same ledger cycle. Payroll engine treated them as separate taxable earnings and applied domestic PAYE in each jurisdiction. Creating ticket PAY-9001 for manual reconciliation, multi-jurisdiction tax credit coordination, and off-cycle refund of the incorrect withholding.

aoife (Payroll): So this is a duplicate-run across providers rather than a withholding "choice". We'll need to coordinate with local Irish payroll to reverse the Ireland PAYE for the UK-seconded days OR apply a foreign tax credit depending on tax residency rules. I'll tag tax-ops and intl-payroll.

neil (People Ops): Do we need Conor's permission to run an off-cycle refund for the Irish PAYE? He needs cash to cover rent next week.

aoife (Payroll): For a clear payroll processing error we do not need employee consent to issue an off-cycle refund. We'll prioritise cash-first: issue immediate off-cycle net refund of the incorrectly withheld Irish PAYE while we reconcile reporting. ETA: within 2 business days to issue refund once ticket triaged. We'll then confirm whether Ireland or UK will ultimately be the reporting jurisdiction for the full pay period and make retrospective adjustments as needed.

liam (Engineer): Will this affect his year-end tax forms in either country? Conor is worried about receiving two sets of tax statements.

aoife (Payroll): Potentially yes. If both jurisdictions withheld and later we reverse one, we'll need to ensure the corrected totals flow into year-end reporting: RTI/P60 for the UK and P60-equivalent or P45 adjustments for Ireland. Ticket PAY-9001 will track whether local payroll needs to issue corrected payslips/P60s or whether we must submit revenue amendments. We'll also coordinate foreign tax credit documentation for Conor.

intl-payroll: Tagging tax-ops now. We should check secondment policy: if Conor remained tax resident in Ireland for part of the period, double withholding may be correct initially but should be addressed by credit or relief. However, because both providers exported lines for the same calendar days, it's likely a processing overlap rather than intended split.

neil (People Ops): I'll DM Conor with the ETA and say payroll is prioritising an off-cycle refund. Please cc me on the ticket and copy tax-ops on final communications.

aoife (Payroll): Will do. Conor, if you can DM a redacted payslip and the secondment letter it will speed review. Also confirm your bank on file for the refund.

conor (via DM to neil): sending redacted stub now, thanks everyone.

payroll-bot: PAY-9001 created: "Duplicate jurisdiction withholding - Ireland/UK secondment ingestion overlap." Priority: High. Assignees: Intl Payroll, Tax Ops.

aoife (Payroll): One quick note for ops: we'll also review our export cutoff windows and provider overlap rules. If two providers export for the same calendar window we should fail the cycle and flag for manual review rather than ingest both. I'll escalate to infra.
